# Results — Study 855 (Accrual Quality, Dechow-Dichev)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **earnings
whose accruals map poorly into operating cash flows are low-quality; sort on accrual quality,
long high-quality (low residual vol) / short low-quality (high residual vol), and the spread
should be positive** (the "low quality is discounted / less persistent" thesis). Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
Sample as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Prices fingerprint `f0610f2cc06e` (yfinance daily adjusted closes); events cache =
2,066 (ticker, filing) rows. Fingerprint `f0610f2cc06e`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **45** deep-history US **non-financial** large filers (fixed, current survivors); 42 clear the DD data bar |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: quarterly `NetIncomeLoss` and `NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities` (reconstructed from the YTD cumulative chain), instant `Assets` (scaling) + `AccountsReceivableNetCurrent` / `InventoryNet` (a working-capital-accrual variant); de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **2,066** accrual-quality quarters across **42** names, period ends **2010-10-31 → 2026-03-31**, stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 45 names, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Primary signal | `aq_vol` = std of the residual from regressing `(NI−CFO)/avg-assets` on lag/current/lead `CFO/avg-assets` over a rolling **12-quarter** window (min 8 usable); `quality = −aq_vol`, so *high quality = low residual vol* |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh `quality` into **terciles**, long top (high quality) / short bottom (low quality), earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Point-in-time guarantee.** The Dechow-Dichev regression uses a *lead* cash-flow term, the
classic look-ahead trap. The rolling window that produces the signal at quarter *q*'s filing
includes only quarters *t* whose full (lag, current, lead) CFO triple is already public on that
filing date — i.e. *t ≤ q−1*, so the last window row's lead is `CFO_q`, disclosed with quarter
*q*. The estimate never peeks past its own filing date.

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** EDGAR reports operating cash flow **year-to-date**
(3/6/9/12-month cumulative), not per quarter, so we reconstruct quarterly CFO by differencing
the cumulative chain. The rolling 12-quarter DD window then needs ~4 years of clean history
before the first signal, and the monthly cross-section grows from ≈26 names (2012) to ≈40
(2024+); the early cross-section is thinner (min 7). Financials are excluded on purpose (the DD
current-accruals model is written for operating firms). No survivorship correction: the basket
is current survivors — named on the Signal axis.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (does accrual quality predict returns?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `quality` (long high-quality / short low-quality), one
execution lag, 2011-05 → 2026-06 (**182 months**, avg cross-section 33.5 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **−3.6 bps/month** (−0.44%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | −0.19 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **−0.18** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | −0.05 |
| monthly hit rate | 49% |
| long leg / short leg | +124.3 / +127.9 bps/month |
| growth of \$1 (gross) | ×0.88 over 182 months |

The spread is **economically zero and, if anything, faintly the *wrong* sign**: the low-quality
(short) leg out-earns the high-quality (long) leg by a hair, so buying quality *loses* a trivial
−0.44%/yr on the autocorrelation-robust statistic (**NW *t* = −0.18**). A staleness-120 variant
is the same picture (−6.7 bps, NW *t* = −0.33). The **working-capital-accrual** variant (residual
vol of `(ΔReceivables+ΔInventory)/avg-assets`) agrees: −10.7 bps/month, **NW *t* = −0.47**. No
specification reaches even |*t*| = 1, let alone the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar.

Note the *direction*: the accrual-quality **factor** literature (Francis et al. 2005) argues
poor quality earns a **risk premium** — low-quality names should earn *more*, which is exactly
the faint tilt here. So the stated "low quality is discounted, buy quality" claim is not merely
uncertified; the sliver of signal that exists leans the other way. Either way it is
indistinguishable from zero.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by quality)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `quality`; top-minus-bottom (high-quality minus
low-quality) forward drift, entered one day after the filing:

| horizon | n | top (high-Q) | bottom (low-Q) | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 2,066 | +1.01% | +1.25% | **−0.24%** | −0.58 | 51% | 0.73 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 2,038 | +3.40% | +3.96% | **−0.56%** | −0.79 | 52% | 0.80 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 1,999 | +7.19% | +8.17% | **−0.98%** | −0.91 | 53% | 0.84 |

Consistently, mildly negative at **every** horizon — the high-quality names slightly *under*-earn
the low-quality names, and the gap grows with horizon (the risk-premium direction again). The
tercile means are **non-monotone** (63 d: +3.96% / +3.36% / +3.40% low→high quality), the
long-short *t* never exceeds −0.91, and the label-shuffle placebo *p* sits at 0.73-0.84 (the
observed long-short is in the *left* tail of a random relabelling). There is **no positive
forward-return sort** in accrual quality on this tape.

## Era split — no regime rescues it

Calendar long-short, split at 2018-01-01:

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| pre-2018 | 80 | +0.4 bps | +0.02 |
| 2018-2026 | 102 | −6.8 bps | −0.23 |

Dead flat early, faintly negative late; neither era carries a certifiable positive. There is no
live-then-arbitraged edge — the return spread never existed.

## The mechanism, though, is real — poor accrual quality **does** flag worse earnings

This is the Dechow-Dichev *validity* claim, and it holds decisively. Split the 2,066 events into
terciles by residual vol; within the best- and worst-quality terciles regress next-quarter ROA
on current ROA (the persistence slope), and compare earnings volatility:

| quantity | good quality (low vol) | poor quality (high vol) |
|---|--:|--:|
| ROA persistence slope (next-q ROA on ROA) | **+0.870** (*t* +19.97) | **+0.273** (*t* +8.59) |
| mean earnings volatility (σ of ROA / assets) | **0.53%** | **2.44%** |

Good-quality earnings are **far more persistent** (+0.87 vs +0.27 quarter-over-quarter carry)
and roughly **5× less volatile** than poor-quality earnings. The accrual-quality construct is
exactly what Dechow-Dichev say it is — a clean, mechanical sort on how noisy a firm's earnings
are. (The persistence *t*'s are pooled across clustered filings; read the magnitude of the gap,
not the literal *t*.) The construct is validated; it simply does not convert into a forward-return
edge, because "this firm has noisier earnings" is a public, slow-moving fundamental the market
already prices.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + quality-signal panel with a TUNABLE planted relation (high-quality names
drift up); no network. Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **+0.10** (sd 1.08), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **1/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 855) | **+23.79** (mean +982.0 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null (one borderline crossing in twelve HAC *t*'s, ~as expected
by chance) and lights up hard on a planted relation. The real-tape NW *t* = −0.18 is therefore a
genuine null, not a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.07):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | −9.2 bps/mo | −1.10%/yr | −0.46 | −0.12 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | −14.7 bps/mo | −1.77%/yr | −0.73 | −0.20 |

The gross spread was already wrong-signed and insignificant; costs only push it further
negative. There is nothing to trade.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The long-high-quality / short-low-quality spread is **economically zero and
  faintly wrong-signed** (−3.6 bps/mo, NW *t* = −0.18; one-sample −0.19), the pooled event drift
  is **negative and non-monotone at every horizon** (long-short *t* −0.58 → −0.91, placebo *p*
  0.73-0.84), the working-capital variant agrees (NW *t* = −0.47), and neither era certifies. The
  stated "buy quality, it's underpriced" claim fails outright; the sliver of tilt that exists is
  the *opposite* (risk-premium) sign.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of realistic long-short costs + borrow the book is −0.46 to
  −0.73 *t*, Sharpe ≈ −0.2. No paycheck — you would pay to hold it.
- **"Does accrual quality flag earnings quality?" — CONFIRMED.** The Dechow-Dichev construct is
  real: good-quality (low residual-vol) names have far more persistent earnings (+0.87 vs +0.27)
  and ~5× lower earnings volatility. The measurement works; the *market* already prices the
  fundamental, so it does **not** become a forward-return edge. Real accounting information, no
  alpha in the stock.
